a: Ruler 4 ascended to power in 708 at a very young age. Three years afterward, in 711, while he was still a child, Toniná secured a significant victory over Palenque. The battle led to the capture of Palenque's ruler, Kan Joy Chitam II, and established Toniná as the dominant centre in the lower Usumacinta region. So decisive was the triumph that it produced a ten-year gap in the dynastic record of the defeated city, a period during which the captured ruler may have been kept as a hostage. Ruler 4 remained in power long enough to mark the period endings of 716 and 721. One captive portrayed on a monument of his is identified as originating from the far-off city of Calakmul, one of the two Maya "superpowers."

a: Each Christmas season, the city of Sarnia stages its annual "Celebration of Lights" in Centennial Park. The event was established in 1984 by Dr. Wills Rawana together with a committee, with funding provided by the retail chain Hudson's Bay and the national telecommunications company Telus. From its modest origins the event has grown considerably and earned numerous honours along the way, among them second place in the 2002 Canadian Government's Canada WinterLights competition. The Celebration was incorporated in that nationally award-winning year and is today managed by a voluntary Board of Directors.

a: Proteins were identified as a separate class of biological molecules in the eighteenth century by Antoine Fourcroy and others, who set them apart by their capacity to coagulate or flocculate when subjected to heat or acid. Among the well-known examples cited at that time were albumin from egg whites, blood serum albumin, fibrin, and wheat gluten.

a: Hentz placed A. sexpunctatus within the subgeneric group Pugnatoriae, made up of jumping spiders in which the first pair of legs was the longest, with the fourth pair next in length. Subsequent entomologists discarded this classification, which Hentz himself conceded was "somewhat artificial." In 1888, once Zygoballus was recognized as a separate genus, the American arachnologists George and Elizabeth Peckham reclassified the spider as Zygoballus sexpunctatus. Specimens of Z. sexpunctatus are held at the Museum of Comparative Zoology, the British Museum, the Milwaukee Public Museum, the American Museum of Natural History, and the Muséum National d'Histoire Naturelle. No type specimens are known to survive.
h: Hentz classified A. sexpunctatus in the subgeneric group Pugnatoriae , which consisted of jumping spiders whose first pair of legs were the longest , followed by the fourth pair . a: Although Lt Col Newman aboard the MGB was under no obligation to go ashore, he was among the first to do so. Newman set up a defence that managed to hold off the growing number of German reinforcements until the demolition parties had finished their work.

a: Towns in the eastern Dominican Republic began making preparations for tens of thousands of refugees, and by 16 January hospitals near the border had been filled beyond capacity with Haitians. By 17 January some reported that they had exhausted supplies of essential medical materials such as antibiotics. Dominican soldiers reinforced the border, and the Dominican Republic's government declared that any Haitians who crossed for medical care would be permitted to remain only on a temporary basis. A local governor remarked, "We have a great desire and we will do everything humanly possible to help Haitian families. But we have our limitations with respect to food and medicine. We need the helping hand of other countries in the area."

a: The Shaoguan incident was a civil disturbance that unfolded over the night of 25–26 June 2009 in Guangdong province, China. A violent confrontation broke out between migrant Uyghur and Han workers at a toy factory in Shaoguan, triggered by allegations that a Han woman had been sexually assaulted. Groups of Han attacked their Uyghur co-workers, resulting in the deaths of at least two Uyghurs (Uyghur workers who witnessed the events report at least 100 killed and 400 wounded) and injuries to some 118 people.

a: Protein folding and binding can be modelled through techniques such as molecular mechanics—particularly molecular dynamics and Monte Carlo methods—which increasingly draw on parallel and distributed computing (the Folding@home project; molecular modeling on GPU). a: A chapel stands at the northern end of the small courtyard, while an esplanade occupies the southern end. The esplanade sits higher than the rest of the courtyard, and the vaulted space beneath it would have served for storage and may have functioned as stabling and as protection from missiles. The hall of the Knights runs along the western side of the courtyard. Although it was probably first constructed in the 12th century, its interior dates to a 13th-century remodelling. The tracery and refined ornamentation represent a sophisticated example of Gothic architecture, most likely from the 1230s.
